examples.ko: 그분은 결단성이 있어서 회의가 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: He is decisive, so meetings end quickly.
A decisive leader is strong in a crisis.
You are kind, but you lack a bit of decisiveness.

examples.ko: 결단성 있게 행동해야 기회를 잡을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to act decisively to seize the chance.
He relied on his decisiveness alone and rushed the work.

examples.ko: 우유부단한 사람이 결단성을 기르는 방법이 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder how an indecisive person can build decisiveness.

explain: 주로 '결단성이 있다/없다'로 써요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '우유부단하다'예요. '결단력'은 결단을 내리는 힘이고, '결단성'은 단호하게 결단을 내리는 성질이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '결단성이 있다/없다', and the opposite idea is '우유부단하다'. '결단력' is the power to make a decision, while '결단성' is the quality of deciding firmly.

en: to be very odd; to be quite strange

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 괴상망측한 옷을 입고 다녀요.
examples.en: That person always goes around in really weird clothes.
The dream was so bizarre that I still remembered it in the morning.

examples.ko: 이 요리는 모양이 괴상망측하지만 맛은 좋아요.
examples.en: This dish looks very strange, but it tastes good.
Why are you making such a weird noise?

examples.ko: 옆집 개 짖는 소리가 괴상망측해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The next-door dog's bark sounded so strange that I was startled.

examples.ko: 친구가 괴상망측하게 웃어서 모두 따라 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend laughed in such a weird way that everyone laughed along.

explain: '이상하다'를 아주 세게 말하는 표현이라 놀라거나 어이없을 때 써요. 좋지 않은 느낌이 많지만 웃긴 상황에도 쓸 수 있어요. 말할 때는 '괴상하다'나 '이상하다'가 더 가볍고 흔해요.
explain_en: It is a very strong way to say '이상하다', used when you are shocked or baffled. It often feels negative but can also be used in funny situations. In conversation, '괴상하다' or '이상하다' sounds lighter and more common.

examples.en: Sweat is glistening on his forehead.
After eating chicken, my mouth is all greasy.
The new car shines glossily in the sunlight.
Because of the oil, your face looks shiny.
I polished my shoes until they gleamed and wore them out.

examples.ko: 번들번들한 책상 위에 먼지가 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: There isn't any dust on the glossy desk.

explain: 기름기나 윤기로 표면이 매끈하게 빛나는 모양이에요. 사람 얼굴에 쓰면 기름져 보인다는 느낌이 있어서 칭찬으로는 잘 쓰지 않아요. '번들거리다'와 같은 계열의 말이에요.
explain_en: It shows a surface shining smoothly from oil or gloss. Used for a person's face, it suggests an oily look, so it is not used as a compliment. It belongs to the same family as '번들거리다'.

en: to be irksome; to be annoying; to be complicated

examples.ko: 번잡한 도심을 벗어나 한적한 시골길을 달렸어요.
examples.en: I left the busy city center and drove along a quiet country road.
This station is too crowded and hectic on weekends.
The market is hectic, but it is lively.

examples.ko: 차가 번잡한 시내로 들어서자 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: As we entered the busy downtown, the road got jammed.

examples.ko: 절차가 번잡해서 서류를 여러 번 냈어요.
examples.en: The procedure was troublesome, so I submitted the documents several times.

examples.ko: 번잡하지 않은 곳에서 조용히 쉬고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to rest quietly somewhere that is not hectic.

explain: 사람이나 차가 많아서 정신없고 어수선한 곳을 말할 때 자주 써요. 반대말은 '한적하다'예요. 절차나 일이 복잡하고 귀찮을 때도 쓰지만, 그냥 '복잡하다'보다 붐비고 번거로운 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is often used for places that feel noisy and chaotic because of many people or cars. Its opposite is '한적하다' (quiet and peaceful). It can also describe procedures or tasks that are complicated and bothersome, with more of a crowded, hassle-filled feel than plain '복잡하다'.

en: to be imperfect; to be incomplete

examples.ko: 이 설명은 아직 불완전해서 더 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: This explanation is still incomplete, so I need to fix it more.
Everyone is an imperfect being.
The data is incomplete, so it is hard to trust the result.
That machine still works imperfectly.

examples.ko: 불완전한 문장은 시험에서 점수를 못 받아요.
examples.en: An incomplete sentence gets no points on the exam.
My first draft is imperfect, but that is okay.

explain: '완전하다'의 반대말이에요. 사람, 제도, 자료처럼 갖춰야 할 것이 덜 갖춰져서 부족한 부분이 있을 때 써요. '미완성'은 아직 다 못 만든 결과물을 말하는 명사라서 '불완전한 글'과 '미완성인 글'은 느낌이 조금 달라요. 일상에서는 '부족하다', '덜 됐다'를 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of 완전하다. It is used for people, systems, or data that lack something they should have. 미완성 is a noun for a work not yet finished, so 불완전한 글 and 미완성인 글 feel a little different. In daily talk people say 부족하다 or 덜 됐다.

examples.ko: 어정쩡한 태도로는 협상에서 원하는 것을 얻기 어려워요.
examples.en: With a wishy-washy attitude, it's hard to get what you want in a negotiation.

examples.ko: 점심을 먹기에는 이르고 간식을 먹기에는 늦은 어정쩡한 시간이에요.
examples.en: It's an in-between time, too early for lunch and too late for a snack.
The clothes are awkwardly big, so they're uncomfortable to wear.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이에서 어정쩡하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I stood awkwardly in between the two people.
I gave a vague answer and caused a misunderstanding.

examples.ko: 어정쩡한 자세로 오래 앉아 있었더니 허리가 아파요.
examples.en: I sat in an awkward position for a long time, and now my back hurts.

explain: 이쪽도 저쪽도 아닌 애매한 상태나 태도를 말할 때 써요. 보통 '어정쩡한', '어정쩡하게', '어정쩡해요'처럼 '-하다'가 붙은 꼴로 써요. 대답, 태도, 크기, 자세, 시간 등에 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a state or attitude that is neither one thing nor the other. It is normally used with '-하다' attached, as in '어정쩡한', '어정쩡하게' and '어정쩡해요'. It can describe answers, attitudes, sizes, postures and times.

en: to be stubborn; to be obstinate

examples.en: His excuse sounds way too forced.
The story in the movie felt contrived, so it was boring.
It was an unreasonable request, so I turned it down.
You don't have to force a smile like that.

examples.ko: 이 광고는 설명이 좀 억지스럽지 않아요?
examples.en: Doesn't the explanation in this ad feel a bit far-fetched?

examples.ko: 친구의 농담이 억지스러웠지만 모두 웃어 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend's joke was forced, but everyone laughed anyway.

explain: '억지스럽다'는 말이나 이야기, 웃음이 무리하게 꾸민 것처럼 보일 때 써요. 고집이 센 사람에게는 '고집스럽다'를 쓰고, 이유나 설정이 안 맞는 것에는 '억지스럽다'를 써요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '억지스러워요', '억지스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: 억지스럽다 fits speech, stories, or smiles that look forced or contrived. For a person who won't change their mind, Koreans say 고집스럽다 instead; 억지스럽다 is for reasons or setups that don't fit. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes 억지스러워요 and 억지스러운.

en: to be old-fashioned; to be typical

examples.ko: 그 영화는 이야기가 너무 진부해서 지루했어요.
examples.en: That movie's story was so clichéd that it was boring.

examples.ko: 진부한 표현은 피하고 새롭게 써 보세요.
examples.en: Avoid clichéd expressions and try writing something fresh.
These days that kind of ad feels stale.
Isn't this idea a little hackneyed?
The ending was predictable, but the acting was excellent.
Even if my joke is corny, please laugh.

explain: 오래돼서 새롭지 않고 뻔하다는 느낌이라 칭찬이 아니에요. '뻔하다'는 일상에서 더 편하게 쓰고, '진부하다'는 표현이나 내용, 생각을 평가할 때 써요. 반대는 '참신하다'예요.
explain_en: It means something is old, unoriginal and predictable, so it is never praise. '뻔하다' is the easier everyday word, while '진부하다' is used when judging expressions, content or ideas. The opposite is '참신하다' (fresh).

examples.en: My younger sibling is still immature and only plays pranks.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 철없는 말을 자주 해요.
examples.en: That child often says thoughtless things.
I sometimes miss my carefree, naive days.

examples.ko: 스무 살인데 너무 철없이 행동한 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm twenty, but I think I acted too childishly.
My friends tease me for being immature.
I was immature. I'm really sorry.

explain: '철이 없다'와 같은 말이고, 반대말은 '철들다'예요. 나이에 맞지 않게 생각이 어린 사람에게 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 흉보는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is the same as 철이 없다, and the opposite is 철들다. It is used for someone whose thinking is younger than their age. Said about an adult, it sounds like strong criticism.
